profile.campus: The Dalles, Wasco County, Oregon (Google's original self-built data center campus)
profile.address: West 2nd Street, The Dalles, Wasco County, Oregon, 97058
profile.reading: This building is the second of two data center structures Google has built along West 2nd Street on its original Dalles campus, the site where Google began constructing its first self-operated data center in 2006, marking the start of Google building and operating its own data center infrastructure rather than leasing it from third parties. Google's own data center locations page lists Oregon among its earliest and most significant US data center states, and the company has stated it has invested more than $7 billion in Oregon infrastructure since 2006, spread across the multiple buildings that now make up the Dalles campus. Google began construction of a fourth building at the site in 2015, expanding beyond the original two-building footprint reflected in OpenStreetMap's mapping of this location. Google chose The Dalles for its location along the Columbia River, which provided both hydroelectric power access from Bonneville Power Administration dams and river water Google has used for cooling, a choice that later became the subject of a long-running local dispute. Fortune's longform reporting and Oregon Public Broadcasting have both covered tension between Google and the City of The Dalles over how much of the city's water rights the data center campus consumes for cooling, with some residents quoted describing the company's local reputation shifting over nearly two decades of expansion. The Dalles campus predates Google's newer Taylor Lake data center project nearby, and this registry treats the original West 2nd Street buildings and the Taylor Lake buildings as distinct facilities despite sharing the same Wasco County campus and operator. Google has not disclosed which specific building on West 2nd Street this OSM-mapped structure corresponds to, nor its individual power capacity or floor area, consistent with Google's general practice of reporting investment and jobs figures only at the state or metro level rather than per building. This registry records the state-level $7 billion Oregon investment figure as regional context rather than attributing it to any single building, and flags county assessor parcel records as the next real research step for building-specific square footage.

reading.body:
This building is one of two structures Google has mapped at its original West 2nd Street campus in The Dalles, where Google began building its own data center infrastructure in 2006, marking a turning point in how the company sourced computing capacity. Google has not published the individual power capacity or floor area of this building, consistent with its practice of disclosing investment and jobs only at state or metro level, so its specific contribution to AI infrastructure cannot be read from public sources. The county assessor parcel record remains the next research step for building-level specifications.

The Dalles campus sits in Oregon, a state with 8 published megawatt figures among 133 mapped facilities, totaling 156.6 MW of disclosed capacity. This specific building's capacity is not published, so its rank cannot be determined, but the broader West 2nd Street campus has anchored Google's Oregon presence since 2006 and been the site of four building projects to date. Google has stated it has invested more than $7 billion in Oregon infrastructure since the Dalles campus began, spread across multiple buildings at this and other state locations.

The site was chosen for access to hydroelectric power from Bonneville Power Administration dams on the Columbia River and river water for cooling, advantages that have enabled expansion but also generated long-running local disputes over water consumption that Oregon Public Broadcasting and other sources have documented. Wasco County's enterprise zone program has abated local property taxes on Google's investment for years at a time under agreements renewed as each new building came online, a structure local officials credit with sustaining the company's continued expansion at this location since 2006.
